svg.title: Ask two questions: added or taken away, and did the behaviour go up?
svg.desc: Top: the two-by-two table of operant contingencies. Adding something and the behaviour rising is positive reinforcement; taking something away and the behaviour rising is negative reinforcement, which covers both escape and avoidance; adding something and the behaviour falling is positive punishment; taking something away and the behaviour falling is negative punishment. Middle: the four reinforcement schedules drawn as cumulative response curves — variable ratio steepest with no pauses, fixed ratio steep with a pause after each reward, variable interval steady and moderate, fixed interval scalloped. Bottom: the shape of operant extinction, with the burst of harder responding that comes first, and a reminder that the three-term contingency runs antecedent, behaviour, consequence.
svg.text: Ask two questions: added or taken away, and did the behaviour go up?
Positive and negative mean add and subtract — nothing about good or bad
The whole system is one table
Cumulative responses: each schedule has its own signature
ratio schedules pay per response, so they drive the rate up; interval schedules pay per clock tick
variable ratio is both the fastest and the hardest to extinguish — which is what a slot machine runs on
Stop reinforcing and it gets worse first
Everything sits in a three-term contingency
the Sᴰ that says reward is available
